name: Global and custom UI
description: Validate global appearance and custom-sidebar definitions statically, then render them only in an isolated profile.

variants.description: Parse Ghostty/Cmux appearance changes and a custom-sidebar source fixture without loading either into the app.
setup: Load isolated before/after config fixtures for theme, font, opacity, and custom-sidebar settings.
Load a sidebar source fixture bound only to mock workspaces, clock, and pull-request records.
exercise: Validate allowed appearance keys, bounded numeric values, theme names, beta enablement, sidebar syntax, data bindings, and command targets.
Reject filesystem, shell, network, or action targets outside the declared sidebar contract.

assertions.expectation: The fixture changes only the declared theme, font, opacity, and sidebar keys.
The sidebar source uses supported bindings and selects workspaces only through an explicit stable ID.
Validation does not interpret the sidebar, reload config, execute actions, or access live PR data.
No user config path or live application state changes.

cleanup: Verify the normal Cmux and Ghostty config file hashes remain unchanged.

variants.description: Apply appearance and custom-sidebar fixtures to a disposable profile, visually verify live reload, and restore the profile.
setup: Create a dedicated Cmux/Ghostty profile and seed it with known baseline theme, font, opacity, and native sidebar settings.
Install the custom-sidebar fixture and mock PR data only inside that profile.
exercise: Apply the declared appearance changes, reload configuration without restarting, validate and select the custom sidebar, and activate one mock workspace row.
Restore the baseline configuration and native sidebar before ending the run.

assertions.expectation: Theme, font, and opacity change in the dedicated profile without application restart.
The custom sidebar renders mock workspaces, clock, and PR status and selects only the clicked owned workspace.
Normal user config hashes and running normal-profile surfaces remain unchanged.
The dedicated profile returns to its baseline or is deleted completely.

cleanup: Restore the native sidebar and baseline appearance in the dedicated profile, then close its surfaces.
Delete the dedicated profile and mock data after confirming the normal profile was untouched.
